title: CoreWeave: FY2026 CapEx outlook and financing context
happened: CoreWeave’s 10 November Q3 materials set company-defined FY2026 capital expenditures at USD 37–39 billion. Q3 company-defined CapEx was USD 14.511 billion, while cash-flow purchases of PP&E and capitalized internal-use software were USD 9.441 billion; the measures have different bases. The issuer also listed financing transaction amounts.
new_info: The current release restates the prior FY2026 CapEx range as USD 35–39 billion, implying a higher lower bound. The original prior outlook is not independently saved here, so this is a qualified issuer-restated comparison. With no dated pre-release consensus, an earnings surprise is UNKNOWN.
affected: CoreWeave itself: delivery pace, funding need and interest burden remain to be observed.
Equipment and data-center construction suppliers at an industry level: orders are possible, but specific vendor benefit is unverified.
AI cloud customers: potential capacity benefit depends on timely deployment and usable service.
pathways: Planned spending and earlier deployment may create capacity sooner; Q3 cash purchases cannot be subtracted from company-defined CapEx to infer lease assets.
Notes and a loan facility may expand funding access while adding interest or dilution exposure; coupon, yield, spread and all-in cost are not established.
conditions: Infrastructure is delivered and utilized on schedule.
Funding can be drawn when needed and expected cash flow or prepayments arrive.
Equipment supply and power constraints do not materially delay deployment.
counterforces: Earlier spending may pressure cash before revenue is recognized.
Financing terms or interest burden may be more costly than the benefit, and convertible notes may dilute owners.
Demand or delivery could fall short of management expectations.
watch: Future separately reported company-defined CapEx and cash PP&E purchases.
Instrument-level coupon, yield, spread, draw and maturity terms.
Delivered capacity, customer prepayments and actual interest expense.
unknowns: Independent first availability and a qualified pre-release consensus.
The original prior CapEx outlook document.
Coupon, yield, spread and all-in cost for each debt transaction.
Separately quantified finance-lease asset additions, specific vendor benefit and price reaction.
time_note: This analysis was written after the materials were retrieved; it is not a prediction made on 10 November. The same-day presentation has date-only publication timing, so ordering within that day is unproven.
